title: 2013 HMMT November Guts Problem 14
statement: Find all triples of positive integers \((x, y, z)\) such that \(x^{2}+y-z=100\) and \(x+y^{2}-z=124\).

solutions.text:
\((12,13,57)\) Cancel \(z\) to get \(24=(y-x)(y+x-1)\). Since \(x, y\) are positive, we have \(y+x-1 \geq 1+1-1>0\), so \(0<y-x<y+x-1\). But \(y-x\) and \(y+x-1\) have opposite parity, so \((y-x, y+x-1) \in\{(1,24),(3,8)\}\) yields \((y, x) \in\{(13,12),(6,3)\}\).
Finally, \(0<z=x^{2}+y-100\) forces \((x, y, z)=(12,13,57)\).
